newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty slips to record low, depos jump.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty slips to record low, depos jump.

text.p: The Polish zloty fell to its lowest level ever against the currency basket on Tuesday, but did not break strong psychological support equal to the parity rate in thin trade, dealers said.

Dealers said small-scale foreign investor sales of zloty-denominated debt instruments in an effort to withdraw from Central Europe after the Czech crown's drop, created strong currency selling pressure on the market.
"Currency-buying dominated today's session but quotes became very cautious whenever the zloty approached parity levels," said Marcin Trzykowski, forex dealer at PKO SA.
The zloty closed at 0.31/0.24 percent from the trading band centre, weaker than Monday's 0.68/0.59 percent.
It closed at 3.2300/30 to the dollar, down from 3.2060/90 on Monday and at 1.9015/22 to the mark, down from 1.8995/10.
Analysts said that more losses could be in store for the zloty in the near-term, which may spark central bank currency selling interventions to prop up the local currency.
"In the medium-term the outlook is positive for the zloty after a modest weekness in the short-term...with the NBP prepared to act if necessary," said James Oats, economist at UBS in London.

On the money market one-day rates jumped to around the 25-percent lombard rate as large banks hoarded funds on Tuesday and sparked panic-buying to protect average reserve positions before the end of the month.
"One or twp large banks did not place any of their surplus cash on the market and effectively pulled up rates to the lombard rate," one dealer at a Polish bank said.
Overnight and tomorrow/next rates closed at 23.50/24.90 and 24.0/25.1 percent respectively against opening at 21.30.
